Primary key for care_gap
Reference to the care plan that incorporates the actions needed to address this care gap.
Reference to the provider attributed responsibility for closing this care gap (e.g., primary care physician).
Reference to the patient for whom this care gap was identified.
Self-referencing FK on care_gap (superseded_care_gap_id)
Reference to the clinical encounter during which this care gap was identified or addressed.
Diagnosis or condition code (ICD-10-CM or SNOMED CT) that triggers or relates to this care gap, such as the chronic disease driving a recommended intervention.
Date the care gap was satisfied by delivery of the recommended care or otherwise resolved.
Mechanism by which the care gap was determined to be closed, supporting audit and supplemental data reporting.
Indicates whether the patient is currently compliant with the associated quality measure for the measurement period.
Timestamp when this care gap record was first created in the system.
Source system or feed from which the evidence used to identify or close the care gap was derived.
Date by which the recommended care should be delivered to remain compliant with the quality measure.
Reason the care gap is excluded from numerator/denominator consideration, such as a valid clinical or administrative exclusion.
Classification of the care gap by the type of recommended care that is overdue or missing.
Current lifecycle state of the care gap indicating whether the recommended care remains outstanding, is being addressed, or has been satisfied.
Date on which the care gap was first identified through analytics, registry, or clinical review.
Date of the most recent patient outreach attempt related to closing this care gap.
Date the recommended service was most recently delivered, used to determine recurrence intervals for periodic measures.
Standardized quality measure code defining the gap (e.g., HEDIS, CMS eCQM, or MIPS measure identifier) against which compliance is evaluated.
Human-readable name of the quality measure associated with this care gap (e.g., Breast Cancer Screening, HbA1c Control for Diabetes).
Quality program under which the care gap is tracked, such as HEDIS, MIPS, CMS Stars, or ACO measures.
The HEDIS or quality program measurement year to which this care gap applies for reporting and rate calculation.
Status of patient outreach activities undertaken to encourage the patient to obtain the recommended care.
Clinical priority assigned to this care gap to support population health outreach and care management triage.
Procedure, test, or service code (CPT, HCPCS, or LOINC) representing the recommended action that would close the care gap.
Narrative description of the recommended clinical action or intervention required to close the care gap.
Timestamp when this care gap record was last modified, reflecting status changes or new evidence.
Primary key for clinical_nlp_result
Reference to the clinician or coder who reviewed and validated this NLP extraction result.
Reference to the NLP model or pipeline version that generated this extraction result.

Foreign key linking to clinical.note. Business justification: Clinical NLP results are extracted FROM clinical notes; each NLP result row references the source note it was derived from. This replaces the generic clinical_note_id with a proper in-domain FK to cli
Self-referencing FK on clinical_nlp_result (source_clinical_nlp_result_id)
Reference to the source clinical document or note that was processed by the NLP engine to generate this result.
Reference to the clinical encounter context in which the source documentation was created.
Associated value extracted for the concept where applicable, such as dosage for a medication or severity for a problem.
The terminology system that the concept_code belongs to, identifying the vocabulary used for the mapped code.
The standardized terminology code (e.g., SNOMED CT, ICD-10, RxNorm, LOINC) to which the extracted concept was mapped.
Human-readable preferred name of the mapped clinical concept from the source terminology.
Model-assigned probability (0 to 1) indicating confidence that the extracted entity and its mapping are correct.
Date and time when this NLP result record was first captured in the data store.
Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) Concept Unique Identifier assigned to the extracted concept for cross-vocabulary linkage.
Indicates whether the NLP result was derived from a de-identified document under HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination.
Date and time the underlying source clinical document was authored, distinct from when NLP processing occurred.
Category of the clinical concept extracted by the NLP engine, classifying it as a problem, medication, procedure, lab, anatomy, symptom, or other.
The verbatim text span extracted from the clinical document that represents the recognized clinical concept. Contains PHI.
Date and time when the NLP pipeline produced this extraction result from the source document.
ISO 639-1 language code of the source clinical document that was processed.
Name of the natural language processing model or pipeline (e.g., cTAKES, Amazon Comprehend Medical, clinicalBERT) that produced the extraction.
Version label of the NLP model used, supporting reproducibility and result lineage across model upgrades.
Reference to the patient whose clinical documentation was processed to produce this NLP result.
Indicates whether the extracted concept was asserted as negated in the source text (e.g., 'no chest pain'). Critical for accurate clinical interpretation.
The canonical or normalized form of the extracted concept after lexical normalization, used for terminology mapping.
Workflow status of the NLP extraction result indicating its position in the validation and review lifecycle.
Indicates whether the extraction requires human clinician review, typically driven by low confidence or clinical significance.
Date and time when the NLP result was reviewed by a human reviewer.
Name of the document section (e.g., History of Present Illness, Assessment, Medications) in which the concept was found.
The UMLS semantic type (TUI/category) classification of the extracted concept, such as Disease or Syndrome or Pharmacologic Substance.
The full sentence from the source document containing the extracted concept, providing surrounding context. Contains PHI.
Character offset position where the extracted text span ends within the source document.
Character offset position where the extracted text span begins within the source document.
Identifies whether the extracted concept pertains to the patient, a family member, or another subject, derived from contextual assertion analysis.
Temporal assertion of the concept indicating whether it is current, historical, hypothetical, or future-oriented.
Indicates whether the concept was expressed with uncertainty or as a possibility rather than a definitive assertion.
Unit associated with the extracted attribute value (e.g., mg, mmHg, mL), standardized where possible to UCUM.
Date and time when this NLP result record was last modified, for example after review or status change.

Detailed business description of what the entity represents, what clinical or analytical use cases it supports, and how it is intended to be used by ML teams.
Name of the data domain that owns this feature store entity (e.g., clinical), supporting domain-aligned governance and feature ownership.
Date from which this version of the entity definition becomes active and available for feature registration and serving.
Date on which this entity definition ceases to be active; null for currently open-ended definitions.
The externally-known unique business code/reference for this entity grouping, used to register and discover the entity in the catalog (e.g., a fully-qualified entity registration name).
Name of the join/lookup key column that uniquely identifies a row for this entity (e.g., patient_id). Used to join feature tables to training and inference datasets.

Human-readable, snake_case logical name of the feature store entity (e.g., patient_demographics, encounter_visit). Serves as the identity label used by data scientists when referencing feature lookups.
Current lifecycle state of the feature store entity, indicating whether it is available for production feature serving or has been retired.
Categorical classification of the subject the entity represents, segmenting the population of feature entities by clinical subject area.
Number of distinct features currently registered against this entity, a structural fact describing the breadth of the entity's feature coverage.
Fully-qualified Unity Catalog feature table that physically stores feature values keyed by this entity, supporting feature serving for clinical ML workflows.
Timestamp when the entity definition or its metadata was last updated.
Indicates whether features for this entity are published to an online store for low-latency real-time inference (e.g., at point of care).
Name of the data science or data engineering team accountable for stewardship, quality, and lifecycle of this feature store entity.
Principal clinical terminology standard most relevant to features derived for this entity, supporting standardized interpretation of clinical feature values.
Cadence at which feature values for this entity are recomputed and materialized, supporting freshness expectations for clinical ML use cases.
Number of days feature values for this entity are retained before purging, aligned to HIPAA and organizational data retention policy.
Operational system of record (e.g., EHR/EMR) from which the underlying clinical data for this entity's features originates.
Contact email of the designated data steward responsible for governance and access approvals for this entity's features.
Name of the timestamp column used for point-in-time feature lookups, ensuring training data avoids feature leakage for time-aware clinical models.
Semantic version of the entity definition, supporting reproducibility and lineage of features across model training iterations.

Self-referencing FK on genetic_variant (parent_genetic_variant_id)
Pipe- or comma-separated ACMG/AMP evidence criteria codes supporting the classification (e.g., PVS1, PM2, PP3).
Observed alternate (variant) nucleotide sequence at the position.
Disease or clinical condition associated with the variant (e.g., Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome), typically MONDO/OMIM mapped.
Chromosome on which the variant is located (1-22, X, Y, or MT).
ACMG/AMP-aligned clinical interpretation of variant pathogenicity. Critical for clinical decision support and patient genomic reports.
NCBI ClinVar accession/variation identifier linking this variant to curated clinical significance assertions.
Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer identifier for somatic/oncology variants.
External canonical identifier from NCBI dbSNP database (e.g., rs6025) uniquely identifying the variant. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for cross-system genomic interoperability.
Laboratory assay/technology used to detect the variant (NGS panel, whole genome/exome sequencing, Sanger, microarray, PCR).
Narrative summary of the supporting evidence and rationale for the assigned clinical significance.
Computational deleteriousness prediction score (e.g., CADD, REVEL) indicating likely functional impact of the variant.
Stable HGNC numeric identifier for the affected gene, enabling unambiguous gene linkage independent of symbol changes.
Approved HGNC gene symbol in which the variant occurs (e.g., BRCA1, TP53). Key classification for clinical interpretation and reporting.
1-based genomic end coordinate of the variant on the reference assembly (equal to start for SNVs).
1-based genomic start coordinate of the variant on the reference assembly.
HGVS coding-level description of the variant relative to the reference transcript (e.g., c.5946delT).
HGVS protein-level description of the predicted amino acid change (e.g., p.Ser1982ArgfsTer22).
Genetic inheritance pattern associated with the variant or its disease association.
Name of the molecular/genetics laboratory that performed the variant interpretation.
Current lifecycle state of the variant interpretation record. LIFECYCLE_STATUS for the resource.
Date the variant classification was last reviewed/curated, supporting reclassification monitoring.
LOINC code for the genetic test observation associated with reporting this variant, supporting clinical interoperability.

Predicted functional consequence using Sequence Ontology terms (e.g., missense_variant, frameshift_variant, splice_donor_variant). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missense|nonsense|frameshift|splice_site|synonymous|intronic|regulatory — promote to reference product]
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man identifier for the associated disease/phenotype.
Indicates whether the variant has documented pharmacogenomic (drug response) relevance per PharmGKB/CPIC guidelines.
PharmGKB accession linking the variant to drug-gene interaction and dosing guidance.
Indicates whether instances of this variant record are linked to identifiable patient genomic data and thus subject to PHI handling controls under HIPAA.
Minor allele frequency observed in reference population databases (e.g., gnomAD), used to assess variant rarity. Principal MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE for the resource.
Reference population database from which the allele frequency was derived.
Name of the in silico prediction tool that produced the functional prediction score.
Timestamp when the variant reference record was first captured in the system.
Reference nucleotide sequence at the variant position per the reference assembly.
Genome build/assembly version against which the genomic coordinates are reported.
SNOMED CT concept identifier representing the variant finding or associated clinical condition.
Indicates whether the variant is inherited (germline), acquired (somatic), or mosaic. Drives oncology vs hereditary reporting workflows.
RefSeq or Ensembl transcript accession (e.g., NM_007294.4) used as the reference sequence for HGVS coding annotation.
Human-readable canonical name or HGVS description of the variant (e.g., NM_000059.3:c.5946delT). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for the resource.
Molecular category of the variant (single nucleotide variant, insertion, deletion, indel, copy number variation, structural). Primary CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE field.
Default or representative zygosity state of the variant when observed in a patient sample.

Clinical decision-support use case the inference supports (e.g., sepsis prediction, fall risk, length-of-stay forecast).
Indicates whether a clinician overrode or rejected the model recommendation, supporting human-in-the-loop governance and adoption analysis.

Indicates whether input feature distribution drift was detected for this inference relative to the training baseline.
Quantitative measure of input or prediction drift computed for monitoring model degradation over time.
Diagnostic message captured when the inference failed or returned an exception, supporting operational troubleshooting.
Interpretability technique applied to generate feature-attribution explanations for this clinical inference.
Version of the feature pipeline or feature store schema used to build inputs, ensuring reproducibility of the inference.
Elapsed time in milliseconds to compute the prediction, supporting performance and SLA monitoring of clinical serving infrastructure.
Outcome status of the inference execution, distinguishing successful predictions from failures or fallbacks.
Precise timestamp at which the model produced the prediction. The principal real-world event time for this log record.
Mode in which the inference was executed: real-time online call, batch scoring, streaming, or shadow evaluation.
Number of input features supplied to the model for this inference, supporting completeness and drift monitoring.

Operating threshold applied to the score to derive the binary or categorical clinical decision at inference time.
Regulatory classification of the model under SaMD / clinical decision-support rules, governing oversight and audit obligations for the inference.
Timestamp when the inference request was received by the serving endpoint, used to derive end-to-end latency.

Indicates whether the patient left the ED Against Medical Advice (AMA) after triage but before completing the full ED visit. Distinct from LWBS — AMA occurs after provider contact. Used for risk management, quality reporting, and EMTALA compliance.

Method by which the patient arrived at the ED or urgent care facility. Includes ground ambulance, air transport (helicopter), walk-in, police transport, private vehicle, or inter-facility transfer. Used for EMTALA compliance, acuity benchmarking, and EMS coordination analytics.

Free-text or structured description of the patient's primary reason for presenting to the ED or urgent care, as stated by the patient or documented by the triage nurse. Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA. Used for clinical documentation, coding, and population health analytics.

Standardized SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) code representing the chief complaint. Enables structured clinical analytics, interoperability, and population health reporting across systems.
Diastolic blood pressure measurement recorded at triage, expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). Used alongside systolic BP for hemodynamic assessment and ESI acuity scoring. PHI under HIPAA.
Date and time the patient physically arrived at the ED or urgent care facility (door time). Used as the baseline for door-to-triage and door-to-provider time quality measures reported to CMS.

Emergency Severity Index (ESI) triage acuity score assigned by the triage nurse, ranging from 1 (most critical/immediate) to 5 (least urgent/non-urgent). Drives resource allocation, bed assignment priority, and ED throughput analytics. Defined by AHRQ ESI Triage Algorithm.

Total Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score assessed at triage, ranging from 3 (deep unconsciousness) to 15 (fully alert). Used for neurological status assessment, ESI acuity determination, and trauma triage protocols. PHI under HIPAA.

business_glossary_term: Heart Rate (HR) in Beats Per Minute (BPM)

Primary language for which interpretation services are required, using ISO 639-1 two-letter language codes (e.g., 'es' for Spanish, 'zh' for Chinese). Supports LEP compliance reporting and interpreter resource planning.

Indicates whether the patient requires isolation precautions at triage (e.g., airborne, droplet, contact, or neutropenic precautions). Drives bed assignment workflows, infection control protocols, and Healthcare-Associated Infection (HAI) prevention measures.
Type of isolation precaution required for the patient as determined at triage. Drives room assignment, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and infection control workflows.

Indicates whether the patient left the ED without being seen by a provider after triage (LWBS). Key ED throughput quality metric reported to CMS and used for EMTALA compliance monitoring and operational improvement initiatives.

Date and time the patient departed the ED without being seen by a provider, when the LWBS flag is true. Used to calculate time-to-LWBS and identify peak demand periods contributing to patient walkouts.

Indicates whether the patient's chief complaint or triage assessment involves a primary mental health or behavioral health concern. Used for ED behavioral health throughput analytics, psychiatric bed management, and EMTALA psychiatric screening compliance.

Type of validated pain assessment scale used to obtain the pain score at triage. Distinguishes between numeric rating scale (NRS), Wong-Baker FACES (pediatric), FLACC (non-verbal), verbal descriptor, or behavioral observation scales.

Patient-reported pain intensity score at triage, typically on a 0–10 numeric rating scale (NRS) or equivalent validated scale (e.g., Wong-Baker FACES for pediatric patients). Used for ESI acuity determination and Joint Commission pain management compliance. PHI under HIPAA.

Date and time when this triage assessment record was most recently modified in the source system. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.

business_glossary_term: Respiratory Rate (RR) in Breaths Per Minute
description: Respiratory rate measured at triage, expressed in breaths per minute. Used for ESI acuity scoring and identification of respiratory distress. PHI under HIPAA.

Indicates whether a sepsis screening alert was triggered at triage based on vital signs and clinical criteria (e.g., SIRS criteria, qSOFA). Supports SEP-1 bundle compliance reporting to CMS and Joint Commission sepsis quality measures.

Native record identifier from the originating operational system (Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED) for this triage assessment. Enables cross-system traceability and supports Health Information Exchange (HIE) reconciliation.
Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) measured by pulse oximetry at triage, expressed as a percentage. Critical indicator for respiratory status and ESI acuity level assignment. PHI under HIPAA.

Indicates whether a stroke alert protocol was activated at triage based on presenting symptoms (e.g., FAST criteria). Supports door-to-CT and door-to-needle time quality measures for stroke care reported to The Joint Commission and CMS.
Systolic blood pressure measurement recorded at triage, expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg). Critical vital sign for ESI acuity determination and clinical decision support. PHI under HIPAA.
Body temperature measured at triage, expressed in degrees Celsius. Used for ESI acuity determination, sepsis screening, and infection surveillance. PHI under HIPAA.
Anatomical route used to obtain the body temperature measurement at triage (e.g., oral, rectal, axillary, tympanic, temporal). Affects clinical interpretation of temperature values.
Indicates whether a trauma team activation was initiated at or following triage. Used for trauma registry reporting, ACS trauma center verification, and ED resource utilization analytics.

Level of trauma team activation triggered at triage (Level 1 = full activation for most critical injuries, Level 2 = partial activation, Level 3 = consult/standby). Drives resource deployment and trauma registry classification.
Categorical classification of triage acuity corresponding to the ESI level. Supports ED throughput reporting, staffing models, and payer analytics. Values align with standard ED triage nomenclature.
Date and time when the triage assessment was fully documented and completed by the triage nurse. Used to calculate triage duration and nurse productivity metrics.

Externally visible, human-readable identifier for the triage assessment record as assigned by the source system (Epic ClinDoc or Cerner PowerChart ED). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trails.

Indicates whether this triage record represents a reassessment of a previously triaged patient (e.g., patient condition changed while waiting). Supports tracking of acuity escalation events and waiting room safety monitoring.
Current workflow state of the triage assessment record. Indicates whether triage documentation is in progress, finalized, subsequently amended, or voided.
Date and time when the triage assessment was initiated by the triage nurse. This is the principal business event timestamp used to calculate door-to-triage time and ED throughput quality measures.

Indicates whether this ICD-10-CM diagnosis code maps to a CMS Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) used for risk adjustment in Medicare Advantage and ACO programs. business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Code

business_glossary_term: International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision (ICD-10) Diagnosis Description
description: Full clinical description of the ICD-10-CM diagnosis code as defined by the WHO/CMS code set. Provides human-readable context for the coded diagnosis. Used in clinical documentation, reporting, and CDI workflows.

The fiscal year version of the ICD-10-CM code set used to assign this diagnosis code (e.g., FY2024). ICD-10-CM is updated annually by CMS/CDC. Ensures accurate code interpretation across fiscal year transitions and supports historical data analysis.

Indicates whether this diagnosis is classified as a mental health or behavioral health condition per ICD-10-CM Chapter 5 (F-codes). True = mental/behavioral health diagnosis. Supports behavioral health program management, parity compliance reporting, and population health segmentation.

The date on which the diagnosed condition first manifested or was first identified, as documented in the clinical record. Supports longitudinal disease tracking, chronic condition management, POA determination, and population health analytics. Aligns with BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP canonical category.

Indicates whether the diagnosis condition was present at the time of inpatient admission. Values: Y=Yes (present on admission), N=No (not present on admission), U=Unknown, W=Clinically undetermined, 1=Exempt from POA reporting. Required by CMS for inpatient claims on UB-04. Impacts HAI reporting, VBP penalties, and hospital-acquired condition (HAC) payment adjustments.

Indicates whether this diagnosis is designated as the primary/principal diagnosis for the encounter. True = primary diagnosis. Provides a quick boolean filter for analytics and reporting without requiring sequence number logic. Complements diagnosis_seq_num and diagnosis_type.

Indicates whether this diagnosis contributes to one or more quality measure denominators or numerators (e.g., HEDIS, MIPS, VBP, TJC core measures). True = this diagnosis is relevant to at least one active quality measure. Supports quality reporting, MIPS scoring, and VBP program management.

Indicates whether this diagnosis is a notifiable/reportable condition requiring mandatory reporting to public health authorities (e.g., state health departments, CDC). True = reportable. Supports public health surveillance, regulatory compliance, and HIE reporting obligations.

The date on which the diagnosed condition was resolved, abated, or no longer active, as documented in the clinical record. Null if the condition is ongoing. Used for chronic disease management, care plan updates, and longitudinal patient health tracking.

Indicates whether this diagnosis code represents a Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) factor (e.g., Z-codes for housing instability, food insecurity, transportation barriers). True = SDOH-related diagnosis. Supports population health management, care coordination, and CMS SDOH reporting initiatives.

Indicates whether this diagnosis represents a substance use disorder (SUD) per ICD-10-CM codes. True = substance use disorder diagnosis. Supports SUD program management, 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality compliance, and population health analytics.

Dollar amount multiplied by total RVU to calculate Medicare payment. Updated annually by CMS. Used in revenue cycle forecasting and contract modeling.

Five-digit numeric code published by the American Medical Association (AMA) that identifies medical, surgical, and diagnostic services. This is the authoritative business identifier used on CMS-1500 claims, in CPOE systems, and for professional billing.

Classification of the CPT code. Category I codes describe established procedures and services. Category II codes are supplemental tracking codes for performance measurement. Category III codes are temporary codes for emerging technology, services, and procedures.

Current lifecycle status of the CPT code. Active codes are valid for billing. Inactive codes have been retired but retained for historical claims. Deleted codes are no longer recognized. Pending codes are scheduled for future activation.
Timestamp when this CPT code record was first created in the enterprise reference data system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

business_glossary_term: CPT (Current Procedural Terminology) Code Effective Date
description: Date on which the CPT code became valid for use in billing and clinical documentation. Typically January 1 of the release year for annual updates.
Indicates whether the CPT code is typically performed in a facility setting (hospital, ASC) or non-facility setting (physician office). Affects practice expense RVU calculation.
Complete clinical description of the procedure or service, including anatomical site, approach, and any modifiers or conditions. Used for clinical documentation, coding review, and CDI workflows.
Indicates whether the procedure is anatomically or clinically specific to male or female patients. Used for claims editing and clinical decision support.

Number of days of post-operative care included in the procedure payment. 000 = endoscopic or minor procedure with 0-day follow-up. 010 = minor procedure with 10-day follow-up. 090 = major surgery with 90-day follow-up. XXX = global concept does not apply. YYY = carrier determines global period. ZZZ = add-on code. MMM = maternity codes with global period. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 000|010|090|XXX|YYY|ZZZ|MMM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Relative Value Unit representing the professional liability insurance component. Reflects the relative risk and cost of malpractice insurance for the service.
Maximum number of units of service that CMS considers medically reasonable for a single patient on a single date of service. Used for claims editing and fraud detection.

Indicates whether bilateral surgery, assistant surgeon, or co-surgeon modifiers are applicable. 0 = not subject to modifier rules. 1 = bilateral surgery applies. 2 = assistant surgeon may not be paid. 3 = assistant surgeon and co-surgeon rules apply. 9 = concept does not apply.

Indicates payment adjustment rules when multiple procedures are performed in the same session. 0 = no payment adjustment. 1 = standard payment adjustment applies. 2 = bilateral adjustment applies. 3 = assistant surgeon adjustment. 4 = diagnostic imaging adjustment. 5 = therapy adjustment. 9 = concept does not apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 0|1|2|3|4|5|9 — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

National average Medicare payment amount for the CPT code, calculated as total RVU multiplied by the conversion factor. Actual payment varies by geographic locality. Used for budgeting and benchmarking.

business_glossary_term: NCCI (National Correct Coding Initiative) Edit Indicator
description: Indicates whether this CPT code is subject to National Correct Coding Initiative edits, which prevent inappropriate code combinations from being billed together. Used for claims scrubbing and compliance.

Level of physician supervision required for the service to be billable. Direct = physician must be present in the room. General = physician must be immediately available. Personal = physician must perform the service. None = no supervision required.
Comma-separated list of valid CMS Place of Service codes where this CPT code may be performed and billed. Used for claims editing and compliance validation.
Relative Value Unit representing the practice expense component, including clinical staff, medical supplies, and equipment costs. Varies by facility vs non-facility setting.

High-level section of the CPT code set to which this code belongs, such as Evaluation and Management, Anesthesia, Surgery, Radiology, Pathology and Laboratory, or Medicine. Used for reporting and analytics grouping.
Abbreviated description of the procedure or service, typically 28 characters or fewer, used in billing systems and charge capture interfaces for space-constrained displays.
Unique identifier for this CPT code in the source system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and troubleshooting integration issues.
Subsection within the CPT section, providing more granular classification such as Digestive System, Cardiovascular System, or Office Visits. Used for clinical analytics and charge capture workflows.
Indicates whether the service can be delivered via telemedicine or telehealth platforms and remain eligible for reimbursement. Updated based on CMS and payer policies.

business_glossary_term: CPT (Current Procedural Terminology) Code Termination Date
description: Date on which the CPT code was retired or deleted from the active code set. Null for currently active codes. Used to prevent billing of obsolete codes and support historical claims adjudication.
Sum of work RVU, practice expense RVU, and malpractice RVU. Used to calculate Medicare reimbursement and benchmark physician productivity.
Timestamp when this CPT code record was last modified in the enterprise reference data system. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

Relative Value Unit representing the physician work component, including time, technical skill, physical effort, mental effort, and judgment required to perform the service. Used in MIPS reporting and physician compensation models.
Unique identifier for the DRG record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: DRG grouper systems (MS-DRG, APR-DRG, AP-DRG) are versioned annually by CMS with fiscal-year-specific relative weights and payment rules. The drg table has grouper_version (STRING), fiscal_year (INT),
Foreign key reference to the parent Major Diagnostic Category under which this DRG is classified.
The arithmetic mean (average) length of stay in days for cases in this DRG. Used for benchmarking and operational performance analysis.
Indicates whether this DRG is included in bundled payment initiatives such as the Bundled Payments for Care Improvement (BPCI) program or Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement (CJR) model.
Grouping of related DRGs into clinical families for service line analysis (e.g., 'Cardiovascular', 'Orthopedic', 'Neurology'). Facilitates portfolio management and strategic planning.

business_glossary_term: Complication or Comorbidity (CC) / Major Complication or Comorbidity (MCC) Level
description: Indicates the severity level of complications or comorbidities included in this DRG definition: without CC/MCC, with CC (moderate complications), or with MCC (major complications). Drives relative weight differentiation.
The dollar threshold above which a case qualifies for additional outlier payment. Calculated as: (DRG payment × fixed loss ratio) + fixed loss amount.
The timestamp when this DRG record was first created in the reference data system. Used for data lineage and historical analysis.
The official numeric code assigned to this DRG by the grouper system (e.g., 470, 871). Used as the business identifier for reimbursement and case mix reporting.
Extended narrative description of the DRG, including clinical context, typical procedures, and coding guidance. Used for clinical documentation improvement (CDI) and coder education.
Classification of the DRG as medical (non-surgical), surgical, or procedure-based. Used for service line segmentation and resource planning.
The date on which this DRG definition and relative weight became effective (typically October 1 of the fiscal year).
The date on which this DRG definition and relative weight expire (typically September 30 of the fiscal year). Null for currently active DRGs.
The geometric mean length of stay in days for cases in this DRG, calculated from national claims data. Used as the threshold for identifying outlier cases and calculating outlier payments.
The DRG grouper classification system under which this DRG is defined: MS-DRG (Medicare Severity), AP-DRG (All Patient), APR-DRG (All Patient Refined), or IR-DRG (International Refined).
The timestamp when this DRG record was last modified in the reference data system. Used for change tracking and audit trails.
The national average total charges (not payments) for cases in this DRG. Used for charge benchmarking and cost-to-charge ratio analysis.
The national average Medicare payment amount for this DRG, calculated as: national base rate × relative weight. Used for benchmarking and financial forecasting.
The total number of Medicare cases nationally that grouped to this DRG in the most recent fiscal year. Used for prevalence analysis and market sizing.
Indicates whether this DRG is classified as an OR procedure DRG, which affects payment and resource allocation.

Indicates whether this DRG is subject to the post-acute care transfer policy, which adjusts payment when a patient is discharged to a post-acute care setting (SNF, IRF, LTCH, HHA) before the geometric mean LOS.
The ending ICD-10-CM diagnosis code in the range of principal diagnoses that can group to this DRG.
The starting ICD-10-CM diagnosis code in the range of principal diagnoses that can group to this DRG. Used for grouper logic validation and clinical documentation improvement.
Indicates whether this DRG requires the presence of a specific ICD-10-PCS procedure code to group (true for surgical DRGs, false for medical DRGs).
Indicates whether this DRG is associated with specific quality measures under the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing (VBP) or Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) Reduction Programs.
Indicates whether this DRG is included in the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP) and subject to payment penalties for excess readmissions.

The DRG relative weight representing the average resource intensity for cases in this DRG compared to the national average (1.0000). Used to calculate expected reimbursement: base rate × relative weight.
Indicates whether this DRG has special payment rules or adjustments (e.g., new technology add-on payments, device-intensive procedures).
The full descriptive title of the DRG (e.g., 'Major Hip and Knee Joint Replacement or Reattachment of Lower Extremity with MCC').

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the HCPCS code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: HCPCS Level II codes are maintained by CMS with annual updates and quarterly releases. The hcpcs_code table has version_year (INT) and status attributes that should be normalized to code_set_version f
Indicates any age-based coverage restrictions for this HCPCS code (e.g., pediatric only, adult only, age 65+). Defines patient age eligibility criteria.
The base unit value assigned to anesthesia-related HCPCS codes, used in calculating anesthesia reimbursement. Null for non-anesthesia codes.
Indicates the payment methodology for this HCPCS code when performed in an Ambulatory Surgical Center setting. Defines whether the code is separately payable, bundled, or excluded from ASC payment.
Indicates whether an assistant surgeon is allowed for this HCPCS code and the applicable payment percentage for assistant surgeon services.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code is eligible for bilateral surgery payment adjustment when performed on both sides of the body during the same operative session.
Indicates whether co-surgeons are allowed for this HCPCS code, where two surgeons perform distinct portions of a complex procedure.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code Type
description: Classification of the code lifecycle: permanent codes are established in the annual update, temporary codes are used for emerging technology or services, deleted codes are no longer valid.

Indicates whether the HCPCS code is covered by Medicare: covered codes are reimbursable, not_covered codes are excluded, carrier_discretion allows local Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) determination, bundled codes are included in other services, conditional codes require specific clinical criteria.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code requires specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes for coverage. True if diagnosis-based medical necessity criteria apply, false otherwise.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code represents durable medical equipment as defined by Medicare. True for DME items (typically E-codes), false for other categories.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code represents a pharmaceutical drug or biological product (typically J-codes). True for drug codes, false for equipment, supplies, and services.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Effective Date
description: The date on which this HCPCS code became valid and available for use in billing and claims submission.
The maximum frequency at which this HCPCS code can be billed (e.g., once per year, once per lifetime, twice per month). Defines time-based coverage restrictions.
Indicates any gender-based restrictions for this HCPCS code. Some codes are specific to male or female anatomy; most have no restriction.
The number of days of post-operative care included in the payment for this HCPCS code (e.g., 000, 010, 090, XXX, YYY, ZZZ). Defines the global surgical package period.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Category
description: The major category of the HCPCS code based on the first letter: A=Transportation/Medical Supplies, B=Enteral/Parenteral, C=Outpatient PPS, D=Dental, E=DME, G=Temporary Procedures, H=Alcohol/Drug, J=Drugs, K=Temporary Codes, L=Orthotics/Prosthetics, M=Medical Services, P=Pathology/Lab, Q=Temporary Codes, R=Diagnostic Radiology, S=Private Payer, T=State Medicaid, V=Vision/Hearing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: A|B|C|D|E|G|H|J|K|L|M|P|Q|R|S|T|V — 17 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code
description: The five-character alphanumeric HCPCS Level II code (e.g., E0601, J1234). First character is always a letter (A-V), followed by four digits. Used to identify durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, supplies, drugs, and non-physician services.
The percentage of the total payment allocated to intraoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.
The date on which this HCPCS code record was last modified in the reference data system, reflecting the most recent change to code attributes, descriptions, or coverage indicators.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Long Description
description: Full detailed description of the HCPCS code, providing comprehensive information about the item, service, drug, or supply represented by the code.
Indicates whether a modifier is required when billing this HCPCS code. True if a modifier is mandatory for proper claims adjudication, false otherwise.
Indicates whether and how payment adjustments apply when this HCPCS code is billed with other procedures on the same date of service. Defines reduction percentages for subsequent procedures.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code has an associated NDC crosswalk mapping. True for drug codes that map to specific NDC products, false otherwise.

business_glossary_term: OPPS (Outpatient Prospective Payment System) Payment Indicator
description: Indicates the payment status for this HCPCS code under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System. Defines whether the code is separately payable, packaged, or excluded from OPPS payment.
Indicates any restrictions on where this HCPCS code may be performed or billed (e.g., inpatient only, outpatient only, office only). Defines valid place of service codes.
The percentage of the total payment allocated to postoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.
The percentage of the total payment allocated to preoperative services for this HCPCS code within the global surgical package.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Pricing Indicator
description: Indicates the pricing methodology for the HCPCS code: fee_schedule uses CMS published rates, asc uses Ambulatory Surgical Center payment, reasonable_charge uses historical pricing, not_priced has no established rate, contractor_priced is determined by local MAC.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code requires prior authorization from the payer before services can be rendered. True if pre-approval is required, false otherwise.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code has separate professional and technical components (e.g., for radiology and pathology services). Defines billing options for split or global billing.
The maximum allowable quantity of this HCPCS code that can be billed per claim, per day, or per time period as defined by coverage policy. Null if no limit applies.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Short Description
description: Abbreviated description of the HCPCS code, typically 28 characters or less, used for display on claims and billing screens.

business_glossary_term: Superseded By HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Code
description: The HCPCS code that replaces this code if it has been superseded or deleted. Null for active codes that have not been replaced.
Indicates whether team surgery is allowed for this HCPCS code, where multiple surgeons of different specialties are medically necessary.
Indicates whether this HCPCS code includes a technical component representing facility resources, equipment, and supplies.

business_glossary_term: HCPCS (Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System) Termination Date
description: The date on which this HCPCS code was discontinued or replaced. Null for currently active codes.
The standard unit of measure for billing this HCPCS code (e.g., each, milligram, milliliter, hour, day, unit). Defines the quantity increment for claims submission.
Primary key for major_diagnostic_category
Self-referencing FK on major_diagnostic_category (parent_major_diagnostic_category_id)
National average length of stay in days for cases grouped to this MDC. Used for benchmarking and utilization management.
Primary anatomical body system or organ system associated with this MDC (e.g., 'Cardiovascular', 'Respiratory', 'Musculoskeletal').
National ranking of this MDC by case volume (1 = highest volume). Used for prioritization and resource planning.
Type of classification logic used for this MDC: organ_system (anatomical), procedure_based (surgical/procedural), condition_based (disease-focused), or special_category (pre-MDC, ungroupable).
Additional clinical context, coding guidance, or special considerations for this MDC. Used by HIM and coding staff.
Type of CC/MCC logic applied within this MDC: standard (uses CC/MCC lists), modified (custom logic), or not_applicable (no CC partitioning).
Total number of DRGs contained within this MDC. Used for reference and validation.
Date when this MDC definition became effective for use in DRG grouping and reimbursement.
Federal fiscal year for which this MDC definition applies (e.g., 2024). CMS updates MDC definitions annually.
Ending ICD-10-CM diagnosis code that maps to this MDC (e.g., 'G99'). Used for grouper logic.
Starting ICD-10-CM diagnosis code that maps to this MDC (e.g., 'G00'). Used for grouper logic.
Ending ICD-10-PCS procedure code that maps to this MDC. Used for surgical partition assignment.
Starting ICD-10-PCS procedure code that maps to this MDC. Used for surgical partition assignment.
Indicates whether this MDC is currently active and available for use in DRG grouping. False for historical or deprecated MDCs.
Date when this MDC record was last modified in the reference data system. Used for change tracking and audit.
Detailed clinical and administrative description of the MDC scope, including typical diagnoses, procedures, and patient populations covered.
Full descriptive name of the major diagnostic category (e.g., 'Diseases and Disorders of the Nervous System').
Current lifecycle status of this MDC in the reference system. Active MDCs are used in current grouper logic.
Standard MDC code used in DRG grouping (e.g., MDC01, MDC02). This is the externally-known unique identifier for the category.
Numeric representation of the MDC (1-25). Used for sorting and grouping logic.
Indicates whether this is a pre-MDC assignment (e.g., transplants, tracheostomy, ECMO) that bypasses standard MDC logic. True for special high-resource cases.
Relative financial impact of this MDC on hospital reimbursement: high (high-cost, high-volume), medium, or low.
Average relative weight of all DRGs within this MDC. Used for cost and resource intensity analysis.
Abbreviated name for display and reporting purposes (e.g., 'Nervous System').
Indicates whether this MDC contains surgical DRGs, medical DRGs, or both. Not applicable for pre-MDC categories.
Date when this MDC definition was retired or superseded. Null for currently active MDCs.
Indicates whether this MDC represents ungroupable cases that do not fit standard classification logic. True for error DRGs.
Version identifier for this MDC definition (e.g., 'FY2024', 'v41.0'). Tracks annual updates to grouper logic.
Unique identifier for the code set version record. Primary key.
Reference to the code_set_version_id of the newer version that replaces this one. Nullable if this is the current active version.
The cryptographic hash algorithm used to generate the file_hash for integrity verification: MD5, SHA256, or SHA512.
The name of the reference code set (e.g., ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, SNOMED CT, LOINC, NDC, RxNorm, DRG Grouper, HL7 Value Set, FHIR Value Set).
The functional category of the code set: diagnosis (ICD-10), procedure (CPT/HCPCS), drug (NDC/RxNorm), observation (LOINC), terminology (SNOMED CT), or grouper (DRG/APR-DRG).
The fiscal or calendar year for which this code set version is required for regulatory compliance and reimbursement (e.g., 2024 for FY2024 ICD-10-CM).
Legal copyright and licensing information for this code set version, including usage restrictions and attribution requirements.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the jurisdiction or country-specific variant of this code set (e.g., USA for ICD-10-CM, CAN for ICD-10-CA).
The date and time when this code set version record was first created in the enterprise reference data repository.
The date and time when this code set version file was downloaded from the source authority.
The date on which this code set version becomes valid and available for use in clinical documentation, billing, and reporting.
Cryptographic hash (SHA-256 or MD5) of the source file, used to verify data integrity and detect unauthorized modifications.
The name of the source file or package containing this code set version (e.g., icd10cm_tabular_2024.xml, cpt_codes_2024.csv).

The file format or data structure of the source code set: csv (comma-separated values), xml (extensible markup language), json (JavaScript object notation), fhir (FHIR CodeSystem resource), hl7 (HL7 v2 table), proprietary (vendor-specific format).

business_glossary_term: Is Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Compliant
description: Indicates whether this code set version meets HIPAA transaction and code set standards for electronic healthcare transactions.
ISO 639-1 two-letter language code indicating the language of the code set descriptions and labels (e.g., en for English, es for Spanish).
The date and time when this code set version record was last modified in the enterprise reference data repository.

The licensing model governing the use of this code set: public_domain (freely available), proprietary (commercial license required), open_source (open license with attribution), restricted (limited use agreement).

The current status of the ETL process for loading this code set version into the enterprise data platform: pending (queued), in_progress (loading), completed (successfully loaded), failed (load error), validated (post-load quality checks passed).
The date and time when this code set version was successfully loaded into the enterprise reference data repository.
The official date on which the source authority published or released this code set version.
The total number of individual codes or entries contained in this code set version.
Summary of changes, additions, deletions, and updates included in this code set version compared to the previous version.
The governing body or organization that publishes and maintains this code set (e.g., WHO, AMA, CMS, SNOMED International, Regenstrief Institute, FDA, NLM).
The official download or reference URL from which this code set version was obtained.
The date on which this code set version is no longer valid for new transactions. Nullable for versions that remain active indefinitely.

The primary business domain(s) for which this code set version is intended: clinical (EHR documentation), billing (claims and revenue cycle), research (clinical trials and studies), quality (HEDIS/quality reporting), or all (enterprise-wide).

The outcome of post-load data quality validation: not_validated (validation not yet performed), passed (all quality checks passed), failed (critical validation errors detected), warning (non-critical issues identified).
The date and time when data quality validation was performed on this code set version.
The official version number or release identifier assigned by the source authority (e.g., 2024, v3.5, FY2024, 20240101).

Current lifecycle status of this code set version: draft (not yet effective), active (currently in use), superseded (replaced by newer version), retired (no longer valid), deprecated (scheduled for retirement).
Unique identifier for the terminology crosswalk mapping record.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: Crosswalk mappings are version-specific - ICD-10-CM to SNOMED CT mappings change with each release of both terminologies. The crosswalk table has source_code_system_version (STRING), target_code_syste
Indicates whether the mapping is an approximate or inexact match (True) requiring clinical review, or an exact semantic match (False).
Indicates whether the target code is one of multiple valid choices for the source code, requiring clinical judgment to select the most appropriate target.
Indicates whether this mapping requires multiple target codes to fully represent the source code (True) or is a single 1:1 or 1:0 mapping (False).
The date and time when this crosswalk mapping record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether the mapping is valid in one direction (forward: source to target only, backward: target to source only) or both directions (bidirectional).
The date on which this crosswalk mapping becomes valid and available for use.
The most recent date on which this mapping was reviewed and validated by clinical or coding subject matter experts.
Grouping identifier for related mappings that should be considered together (e.g., all mappings for a specific clinical domain or use case).
Numeric ranking indicating the preferred order when multiple target codes are valid for a single source code (lower numbers indicate higher priority).
The authoritative source or organization that published or validated this mapping (e.g., CMS, NLM, SNOMED International, Regenstrief Institute, internal clinical terminology team).
The intended use case or business purpose for this mapping (e.g., claims submission, clinical documentation, quality reporting, SDOH screening, interoperability, legacy system migration).
The confidence or precision level of the mapping: exact (perfect semantic match), high (strong clinical equivalence), moderate (acceptable with context), low (weak or conditional match).
Textual description of any conditional logic, clinical context, or business rules that govern when and how this mapping should be applied.

The semantic relationship between source and target codes: equivalent (1:1 exact match), broader (source is more specific than target), narrower (source is more general than target), related (associated but not hierarchical), inexact (approximate match), unmatched (no suitable target).
Indicates whether the source code has no suitable equivalent in the target code system (True) or a valid mapping exists (False).
Free-text field for additional context, clinical guidance, or special instructions related to this mapping.
Identifies specific clinical or billing scenarios where this mapping applies (e.g., inpatient vs outpatient, primary vs secondary diagnosis).
The specific code value in the source code system being mapped from (e.g., E11.9 for ICD-10, 73211009 for SNOMED CT).
Human-readable display text or description for the source code.
The originating terminology or code system from which the mapping is derived (e.g., ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT, CPT, LOINC, NDC, RxNorm).
The specific code value in the target code system being mapped to (e.g., 73211009 for SNOMED CT, 99213 for CPT).
Human-readable display text or description for the target code.
The destination terminology or code system to which the mapping is made (e.g., ICD-10-CM, SNOMED CT, CPT, LOINC, NDC, RxNorm).
The date on which this crosswalk mapping is no longer valid or has been superseded. Null indicates the mapping is still active.
The date and time when this crosswalk mapping record was last modified.
The number of times this crosswalk mapping has been applied in production systems, used for mapping quality assessment and optimization.
The name or identifier of the clinical or coding expert who last validated this mapping.
