business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Value Set Identifier
description: Unique identifier for the FHIR value set record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: FHIR value sets are versioned by HL7 with release-specific canonical URLs and expansion timestamps. The fhir_value_set table has version (STRING) and status attributes that should be normalized to cod
Date when this value set was formally approved by the governance authority for production use. Required for regulatory compliance and change control.

Defines how strictly FHIR resources must conform to this value set. Required = must use codes from this set only, Extensible = should use but may extend, Preferred = recommended but not enforced, Example = illustrative only.
Globally unique canonical URL that permanently identifies this value set across all FHIR implementations. Used for terminology server lookups and resource references.
Number of exclude rules defined in the value set composition. Exclude rules remove specific concepts from the included set.
Number of include rules defined in the value set composition. Each include rule specifies a code system and filter criteria for selecting concepts.
JSON-encoded contact details for the publisher or steward of this value set, including name, email, phone, and URL. Used for support and governance inquiries.
Legal copyright and licensing terms governing the use of this value set. Critical for code systems like SNOMED CT, CPT, and ICD-10 that require licensing agreements.
Date and time when this value set record was first created in the enterprise terminology repository. Audit trail for data lineage.
Date when this value set version is retired and should no longer be used for new data entry. Null indicates the value set is currently active with no planned retirement.
Date when this value set version becomes active and available for use in clinical systems. Part of the temporal validity window.
Unique identifier for the current expansion of this value set. Changes each time the value set is expanded by a terminology server to reflect the current set of member concepts.
Paging offset used when the expansion was generated. Supports large value sets that cannot be returned in a single response.
JSON-encoded parameters used during the expansion operation, such as language, display variant, or active-only filters. Stored as text for auditability.
Date and time when the value set was last expanded by a terminology server to produce the current list of member concepts. Critical for cache invalidation and version control.
Total number of coded concepts included in the current expansion of this value set. Used for validation and performance optimization.
Indicates whether this value set is for testing or experimental purposes and should not be used in production clinical systems. True means not approved for operational use.

business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Element Path
description: Specific element path within the FHIR resource where this value set binding applies, using dot notation. Example: Observation.code, Condition.clinicalStatus, Procedure.category.

business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Resource Type
description: The FHIR resource type that this value set is bound to, such as Observation, Condition, Procedure, MedicationRequest, or AllergyIntolerance. Indicates where this terminology is applied in clinical workflows.
Detailed narrative description of the value set purpose, scope, and intended use cases. Provides clinical and business context for terminology consumers.
Indicates whether the value set definition is immutable and will never change once published. True means the expansion will always produce the same set of codes.
Comma-separated list of ISO 3166 country codes or jurisdiction identifiers where this value set is intended for use. Examples: USA, CAN, GBR. Supports regional terminology requirements.
Date when this value set was last reviewed for clinical accuracy and relevance. Used to trigger periodic re-validation cycles per governance policy.
Date and time when this value set record was last updated in the enterprise terminology repository. Supports change tracking and cache invalidation.
Name of the organization or individual responsible for publishing and maintaining this value set. Examples include HL7, SNOMED International, LOINC, or internal enterprise teams.
Explanation of why this value set was created and the specific clinical or administrative problem it addresses. Helps users understand appropriate usage scenarios.
Human-readable title for the value set displayed in user interfaces and documentation. May contain spaces and special characters.
JSON-encoded array of usage contexts defining when and where this value set should be applied. Includes clinical specialty, care setting, patient demographics, and workflow phase.
Computer-friendly name for the value set, typically used in code generation and system identifiers. Must be alphanumeric without spaces.
ISO object identifier uniquely identifying this value set in the global OID registry. Format follows ISO/IEC 8824 dotted decimal notation.

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the ICD code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS codes are published annually by CMS with version-specific effective/expiration dates. The icd_code table has version (STRING) and status attributes that should be normalized t
The maximum patient age (in years) for which this ICD code is clinically appropriate. Used for coding validation and quality checks. Null if no maximum age restriction applies.
The minimum patient age (in years) for which this ICD code is clinically appropriate. Used for coding validation and quality checks. Null if no minimum age restriction applies.

Indicates whether this ICD code is valid for billing and reimbursement purposes. Only billable codes may be submitted on claims to payers. Non-billable codes are typically higher-level category codes used for classification only.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is classified as a Complication or Comorbidity (CC) for DRG assignment and severity adjustment purposes.

The ICD-10 chapter to which this code belongs, representing the highest-level clinical category (e.g., Chapter 1: Certain infectious and parasitic diseases, Chapter 9: Diseases of the circulatory system).

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Chapter Code Range
description: The alphanumeric range defining the chapter boundaries (e.g., A00-B99 for infectious diseases). Used for hierarchical grouping and reporting.

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Type
description: Indicates whether this code represents a diagnosis (ICD-10-CM) or a procedure (ICD-10-PCS).
The date and time when this ICD code record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
The date on which this ICD code became valid for use in clinical documentation, billing, and reporting. Aligns with annual CMS ICD-10 update cycles (typically October 1).
Indicates whether this code represents the underlying etiology or cause of a condition and should be sequenced before manifestation codes per ICD-10-CM coding conventions.
The date on which this ICD code was retired or replaced and is no longer valid for use. Null for currently active codes.
Indicates whether this ICD code is applicable only to male patients, only to female patients, or to both. Used for clinical validation and coding accuracy.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code represents a Hospital-Acquired Condition (HAC) as defined by CMS. HACs may result in payment penalties under the Hospital-Acquired Condition Reduction Program.
The three-character category code representing a group of related conditions or procedures within a chapter (e.g., A01 for typhoid and paratyphoid fevers).
The full ICD-10-CM diagnosis code or ICD-10-PCS procedure code as published by WHO and maintained by CMS. Format follows alphanumeric pattern with optional decimal subdivision (e.g., A01.0, Z99.89).

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Long Description
description: Full clinical description of the diagnosis or procedure code, providing comprehensive detail for clinical documentation, coding accuracy, and medical record completeness.
Indicates whether this code represents a manifestation of an underlying disease and must be sequenced after the underlying condition code per ICD-10-CM coding conventions.

Indicates whether this diagnosis code is classified as a Major Complication or Comorbidity (MCC) for DRG assignment and severity adjustment purposes. MCCs have greater impact on reimbursement than standard CCs.

business_glossary_term: Parent ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code
description: The immediate parent code in the ICD-10 hierarchy, enabling hierarchical rollup and drill-down navigation for reporting and analytics.
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is exempt from the CMS Present on Admission (POA) reporting requirement for inpatient claims. POA-exempt codes do not require a POA indicator on UB-04 claims.

business_glossary_term: Replacement ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code
description: The ICD code that replaces this code if the code has been retired or superseded. Used for code mapping and historical claims reprocessing.

business_glossary_term: ICD (International Classification of Diseases) Code Short Description
description: Abbreviated clinical description of the diagnosis or procedure code, typically used in constrained display contexts such as billing forms and summary reports.

business_glossary_term: SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) Mapping
description: The corresponding SNOMED CT concept identifier(s) mapped to this ICD code, enabling interoperability with clinical terminology systems and EHR platforms.
The four-character subcategory code providing additional clinical specificity within a category (e.g., A01.0 for typhoid fever).
Indicates whether this diagnosis code is prohibited from being used as the principal diagnosis on an inpatient claim per CMS coding guidelines.
The date and time when this ICD code record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Indicates whether this code is valid for use in clinical documentation and coding. Codes may be invalid due to retirement, replacement, or administrative reasons.

business_glossary_term: LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) Code ID
description: Unique identifier for the LOINC code record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: LOINC codes are maintained by Regenstrief Institute with biannual releases. The loinc_code table has version_first_released (STRING), version_last_changed (STRING), and status attributes that should b
The high-level category or domain of the observation (e.g., CHEM=Chemistry, HEM/BC=Hematology/Blood Count, MICRO=Microbiology, RAD=Radiology, VITALS=Vital Signs).
The substance or entity being measured or observed (e.g., Glucose, Hemoglobin, Creatinine). This is the analyte, the target of the measurement.
A patient-friendly, lay-language name for the observation or test, used in patient portals and consumer-facing applications.
The date and time when this LOINC code record was first created in the system. Audit trail field.
The date when this LOINC code was deprecated or retired. Null if the code is still active.
The preferred display name for this LOINC code in the current implementation. May be customized by the organization while maintaining the standard LOINC number.
The date when this LOINC code became active and available for use in clinical systems.

business_glossary_term: Example UCUM (Unified Code for Units of Measure) Units
description: The standardized UCUM representation of the example units. Used for interoperability and unit conversion.
Common units of measure for this observation (e.g., mg/dL, mmol/L, %). Provides guidance for result reporting.
Copyright or licensing information for LOINC codes that incorporate third-party content (e.g., SNOMED CT, CPT). Required for compliance with external terminology licenses.

business_glossary_term: HL7 (Health Level Seven) Field Subfield ID
description: The HL7 v2.x message field identifier where this LOINC code is typically used (e.g., OBX-3 for observation identifier). Supports HL7 message mapping.

business_glossary_term: HL7 (Health Level Seven) Version 3 Code System OID (Object Identifier)
description: The HL7 v3 object identifier for the LOINC code system (typically 2.16.840.1.113883.6.1). Used in CDA documents and HL7 v3 messages.
Boolean flag indicating whether this LOINC code is currently active and available for use in the organization. True=active, False=inactive or deprecated locally.
The date when this LOINC code mapping was last reviewed and verified by clinical informatics or laboratory staff. Supports ongoing terminology governance.
Organization-specific internal code or identifier mapped to this LOINC code. Used for legacy system integration and local terminology management.

business_glossary_term: LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) Number
description: The unique LOINC code identifier assigned by Regenstrief Institute. Format: numeric-numeric (e.g., 2345-7). This is the authoritative external identifier for the observation or test.
The full, human-readable display name for the LOINC code. This is the primary display term used in clinical systems and reports.
The method or technique used to make the observation or measurement (e.g., Electrophoresis, Immunoassay, Microscopy). May be null if method is not specified.
Indicates whether this LOINC code is used for ordering tests, recording observations, or both. Order=orderable panel or test, Observation=result only, Both=can be used for ordering and results.
Indicates if this LOINC code represents a panel (group of related tests), battery (predefined test group), or set (collection of observations). Null for individual observations.
The characteristic or attribute of the analyte being measured (e.g., Mass Concentration, Substance Concentration, Presence, Volume).
Synonyms, alternate names, or legacy names for this observation. Supports search and mapping from legacy systems.
The scale of measurement for the observation result. Qn=Quantitative (numeric), Ord=Ordinal (ranked), Nom=Nominal (named categories), Nar=Narrative (free text), Doc=Document (attached file).
An abbreviated display name for the LOINC code, used when space is limited in user interfaces or reports.
The source instrument or questionnaire from which the survey question originates (e.g., PHQ-9, PROMIS, CAHPS).
For LOINC codes representing survey or assessment questions, this field contains the full question text as presented to the patient or clinician.
The specimen or body system from which the observation was made (e.g., Blood, Serum, Urine, Plasma, Cerebrospinal fluid).
The time dimension of the measurement (e.g., Point in time, 24 hour, 8 hour). Indicates whether the observation is a single point measurement or collected over a time interval.
The date and time when this LOINC code record was last modified. Audit trail field.
Unique identifier for the NDC drug product record in the enterprise data warehouse.

Foreign key linking to reference.code_set_version. Business justification: NDC drug products are maintained by the FDA with weekly updates to the NDC Directory. The ndc_drug table has ndc_status attribute and marketing_start_date/marketing_end_date that track product lifecyc
The chemical substance or compound responsible for the therapeutic effect of the drug.
The FDA application number associated with the drug approval (e.g., NDA number, ANDA number, BLA number).
The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification code, used internationally for drug classification.
Indicates whether the drug is a biosimilar product, highly similar to an already-approved biological product.
Indicates whether the drug carries an FDA black box warning, the strictest warning for serious or life-threatening risks.
The controlled substance schedule classification assigned by the DEA (CI through CV), indicating the drug's potential for abuse and accepted medical use. Empty if not a controlled substance.
The physical form in which the drug is administered (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, solution, cream, inhaler).
The date on which this NDC drug record became effective in the enterprise reference data system.
The date on which this NDC drug record is no longer valid or was superseded. Null if currently active.

business_glossary_term: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) Medication Code
description: The standardized medication code used in FHIR MedicationRequest and Medication resources for interoperability.
Indicates whether the drug is included in the organization's formulary and any restrictions or preferences applied.
The Medi-Span Generic Product Identifier, a 14-character hierarchical classification code used in pharmacy systems.
Indicates whether the drug is classified as a high-alert medication by ISMP, requiring special handling and verification procedures.
The name of the company or entity that manufactures, repackages, or distributes the drug product.
The regulatory pathway under which the drug was approved (e.g., NDA, ANDA, BLA, OTC Monograph).
The date on which the drug product was discontinued or withdrawn from the market. Null if still active.
The date on which the drug product was first marketed or made available for distribution.
The 11-digit National Drug Code assigned by the FDA, uniquely identifying the labeler, product, and package size. Format: 5-4-2 (labeler-product-package).
The generic or non-proprietary name of the drug, typically the active ingredient name established by the United States Adopted Names (USAN) Council.
The therapeutic equivalence code from the FDA Orange Book, indicating whether a generic drug is therapeutically equivalent to the brand-name drug.
Indicates whether the drug is available for purchase without a prescription.
A textual description of the package size and configuration (e.g., bottle of 100 tablets, box of 10 vials).
The numeric quantity of units contained in the package.
The unit of measure for the package quantity (e.g., tablet, capsule, mL, vial).
The FDA pregnancy category classification indicating the risk of fetal harm (A=safest, X=contraindicated, N=not classified). Note: FDA replaced this with narrative labeling in 2015.
The full product name as registered with the FDA, including strength and dosage form.
The brand or trade name under which the drug is marketed to consumers and healthcare providers.
The timestamp when this NDC drug record was first created in the enterprise data warehouse.
The timestamp when this NDC drug record was last updated in the enterprise data warehouse.
Indicates whether the drug requires refrigerated storage to maintain stability and efficacy.
The path by which the drug is administered into the body (e.g., oral, intravenous, topical, subcutaneous, intramuscular).
The RxNorm Concept Unique Identifier assigned by the National Library of Medicine, providing a normalized drug concept mapping for interoperability.
The normalized drug name as defined in RxNorm, representing the clinical drug concept.
The source vocabulary from which the RxNorm concept was derived (e.g., RXNORM, VANDF, MMSL, NDDF).
Indicates whether the RxNorm concept is suppressed from use (N=not suppressed, Y=suppressed, O=obsolete, E=entry term).
The RxNorm term type classification (e.g., IN for ingredient, BN for brand name, SCD for semantic clinical drug, GPCK for generic pack).

business_glossary_term: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) Code
description: The SNOMED CT concept code representing the drug product or substance for clinical documentation and interoperability.
The concentration or potency of the active ingredient(s) in the drug product, expressed as a numeric value with unit (e.g., 500 mg, 10 mg/mL).
The unit of measure for the drug strength (e.g., mg, mL, mcg, IU, %).
The therapeutic or pharmacological classification of the drug (e.g., antibiotic, antihypertensive, analgesic).
The FDA Unique Ingredient Identifier code for the active ingredient, used for substance identification.
Indicates whether the drug product is a vaccine used for immunization.

business_glossary_term: SNOMED CT (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine Clinical Terms) Concept Identifier
description: Unique identifier for the SNOMED CT concept as assigned by SNOMED International. This is the primary key and corresponds to the SCTID (SNOMED CT Identifier) in the SNOMED CT release files.
The SNOMED CT release version identifier from which this concept was loaded (e.g., '20230901', '2023-09-01'). Supports version tracking and change management across SNOMED CT releases.

Identifier of the immediate parent concept in the SNOMED CT IS-A hierarchy. Used to navigate the taxonomy and determine subsumption relationships. A concept may have multiple parents in a polyhierarchy.

The typical section(s) of clinical documentation where this concept is used (e.g., 'Problem List', 'Allergies', 'Past Medical History', 'Assessment', 'Plan', 'Procedures'). Supports context-aware search and documentation templates.

Additional classification of the concept beyond the semantic tag, used for grouping and filtering (e.g., 'diagnosis', 'symptom', 'surgical procedure', 'medication', 'laboratory test'). May be derived from semantic tag or additional metadata.
A formal textual definition of the concept providing clinical context and meaning. May be sourced from SNOMED International or supplemented with organizational definitions for clarity.

Current lifecycle status of the SNOMED CT concept. Active concepts are available for use in clinical documentation; inactive concepts are deprecated and should not be used for new entries but may appear in historical data.

business_glossary_term: CPT (Current Procedural Terminology) Map Target Code
description: The CPT code(s) to which this SNOMED CT procedure concept is mapped, if applicable. Supports billing and revenue cycle management by linking clinical procedures to reimbursable CPT codes.
The timestamp when this concept record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Indicates whether the concept is primitive (defined only by its stated relationships) or fully defined (sufficient conditions provided for automated classification). Fully defined concepts can be automatically classified by description logic reasoners.

The date on which this version of the concept became effective in the SNOMED CT release. Represents the snapshot date of the concept state in the release cycle (typically in YYYYMMDD format in source, stored as DATE).

business_glossary_term: FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) Value Set Membership
description: Comma-separated list of FHIR value set identifiers (URIs) to which this concept belongs. Used to support FHIR-based interoperability and constrain coded elements in FHIR resources.

The complete, unambiguous name of the SNOMED CT concept including the semantic tag in parentheses (e.g., 'Pneumonia (disorder)'). The FSN uniquely identifies the concept and includes the semantic category to distinguish homonyms.
The depth of this concept in the SNOMED CT hierarchy, with the root concept at level 0. Used for hierarchy traversal, rollup queries, and determining concept granularity.

The correlation type between the SNOMED CT concept and the ICD-10 map target, indicating the semantic equivalence of the mapping (e.g., exact match, SNOMED concept is narrower than ICD-10 code, SNOMED concept is broader, partial overlap, or not mappable).

business_glossary_term: ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases 10th Revision) Map Target Code
description: The ICD-10 code(s) to which this SNOMED CT concept is mapped, if applicable. Supports billing, reporting, and interoperability with systems that use ICD-10 for diagnosis coding. Multiple codes may be pipe-separated.

business_glossary_term: Is EHR (Electronic Health Record) Preferred Concept Flag
description: Boolean flag indicating whether this concept is designated as a preferred term for use in the organization's EHR system. Preferred concepts are promoted in search results and pick lists to standardize documentation.
Boolean flag indicating whether this concept is a leaf node in the hierarchy (has no child concepts). Leaf concepts represent the most granular clinical terms available.

Boolean flag indicating whether the concept is primitive (true) or fully defined (false). Primitive concepts require manual classification; fully defined concepts can be automatically classified by reasoners.

Boolean flag indicating whether this concept represents a condition that must be reported to public health authorities (e.g., notifiable diseases, healthcare-associated infections). Used to trigger automated reporting workflows.
The most recent date on which this concept was used in clinical documentation within the organization. Used to identify obsolete or rarely used concepts for potential retirement or training needs.

business_glossary_term: LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) Map Target Code
description: The LOINC code(s) to which this SNOMED CT concept is mapped, if applicable. Used for laboratory and clinical observations to support interoperability with laboratory information systems and FHIR resources.

Identifier of the SNOMED CT module (namespace) to which this concept belongs. Modules represent different editions or extensions (e.g., International Edition, US Edition, UK Edition) and control versioning and governance.
A simplified, patient-friendly description of the concept for use in patient portals, after-visit summaries, and patient education materials. Avoids medical jargon and uses plain language.

The preferred human-readable term for the concept in the default language (typically English). This is the term most commonly used in clinical documentation and user interfaces, without the semantic tag.

Comma-separated list of quality measure identifiers (e.g., HEDIS, CMS, MIPS) for which this concept is included in the numerator, denominator, or exclusion criteria. Supports automated quality reporting and value-based care programs.
The total number of active relationships (both stated and inferred) associated with this concept. Relationships define the concept's meaning and position in the ontology.

The RxNorm code(s) to which this SNOMED CT pharmaceutical/biologic product concept is mapped, if applicable. Enables medication interoperability and e-prescribing by linking to the NLM RxNorm drug terminology.

The high-level semantic category of the concept extracted from the FSN (e.g., 'disorder', 'procedure', 'finding', 'body structure', 'substance', 'organism'). Used to classify concepts into broad clinical domains.

Comma-separated list of medical specialties for which this concept is particularly relevant (e.g., 'Cardiology', 'Oncology', 'Pediatrics', 'Emergency Medicine'). Used to customize pick lists and search results by provider specialty.
The number of active synonym descriptions associated with this concept. Synonyms provide alternative terms for the same concept to support varied clinical documentation styles and search.

The top-level SNOMED CT hierarchy to which this concept belongs (e.g., 'Clinical Finding', 'Procedure', 'Body Structure', 'Pharmaceutical / Biologic Product', 'Organism', 'Substance', 'Physical Object', 'Qualifier Value', 'Observable Entity', 'Situation', 'Event', 'Environment', 'Social Context', 'Staging and Scales', 'Linkage Concept', 'Special Concept', 'Navigational Concept', 'Record Artifact'). Derived from the root ancestor in the IS-A hierarchy.
The timestamp when this concept record was last updated in the enterprise data platform. Used for change tracking and incremental data processing.
Rank of this concept based on usage frequency in clinical documentation within the organization. Lower numbers indicate higher usage. Used to prioritize search results and optimize user interfaces.
Unique identifier for the geographic region entity. Primary key.
Reference to the parent geographic region in the hierarchy (e.g., a ZIP code's parent county, a county's parent state). Null for top-level regions (e.g., country).

business_glossary_term: Accountable Care Organization (ACO) Service Area Flag
description: Indicates whether this region is part of an ACO service area. True if the region is included in one or more ACO service territories; false otherwise. Used for value-based care program eligibility and population attribution.
The U.S. Census Bureau Core-Based Statistical Area code. Used for metropolitan and micropolitan statistical area analysis, market segmentation, and payer contracting territories.
The human-readable name of the CBSA (e.g., 'New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA'). Null for non-CBSA region types.

The U.S. Census Bureau division classification, a finer granularity than census_region. Values: new_england, middle_atlantic, east_north_central, west_north_central, south_atlantic, east_south_central, west_south_central, mountain, pacific. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_england|middle_atlantic|east_north_central|west_north_central|south_atlantic|east_south_central|west_south_central|mountain|pacific — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The U.S. Census Bureau region classification: northeast, midwest, south, west. Used for demographic and statistical analysis.

business_glossary_term: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Region Number
description: The CMS administrative region number (1-10). Used for regulatory reporting, Quality Payment Program (QPP) reporting, and CMS regional office alignment.
The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX). Used for international patient populations and cross-border care coordination.
The date through which this geographic region record is effective. Null for currently active regions. Used for temporal validity and historical analysis of region definitions.
The date from which this geographic region record is effective. Used for temporal validity and historical analysis of region definitions (e.g., ZIP code boundary changes, CBSA redefinitions).
The Federal Information Processing Standards code for this region. Used for counties (5-digit) and states (2-digit). Null for non-FIPS region types.

The CMS Hospital Referral Region code representing a regional health care market for tertiary medical care. Used for population health management, quality benchmarking, and regional variation analysis.

The CMS Hospital Service Area code representing a collection of ZIP codes whose residents receive most of their hospitalizations from the hospitals in that area. Used for facility service area definitions and market share analysis.
Indicates whether this geographic region record is currently active and valid for use. True if active; false if retired or superseded. Used for address validation and operational reporting.
The timestamp when this geographic region record was last updated in the data platform. Used for data lineage, change tracking, and audit purposes.
The geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees) representing the centroid or representative point of the region. Used for mapping, distance calculations, and geospatial analysis.
The geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees) representing the centroid or representative point of the region. Used for mapping, distance calculations, and geospatial analysis.

The median household income (in USD) for this region, sourced from U.S. Census or American Community Survey data. Used for Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) analysis, financial assistance program eligibility, and health equity reporting.

The estimated total population residing in this geographic region, sourced from the most recent U.S. Census or American Community Survey data. Used for population health stratification, capacity planning, and per-capita rate calculations.
The percentage of the population living below the federal poverty line in this region. Used for SDOH analysis, charity care program targeting, and community health needs assessments.
The standardized code representing this geographic region (e.g., ZIP code, FIPS code, CBSA code, HSA code, HRR code, state abbreviation). Format and length vary by region_type.
The human-readable name of the geographic region (e.g., city name for ZIP, county name, CBSA name, state name).

Discriminator indicating the type of geographic region: zip_code (5-digit ZIP), county, state, cbsa (Core-Based Statistical Area), hsa (Hospital Service Area), hrr (Hospital Referral Region), cms_region (CMS administrative region), aco_service_area (Accountable Care Organization service area), zcta (ZIP Code Tabulation Area), country. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: zip_code|county|state|cbsa|hsa|hrr|cms_region|aco_service_area|zcta|country — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The Rural-Urban Commuting Area code classifying the region by urbanization and commuting patterns. Used for population health stratification and Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) analysis.
The two-letter U.S. state abbreviation (e.g., CA, NY, TX). Populated for U.S. regions; null for non-U.S. or non-state region types.
The IANA time zone identifier for this region (e.g., America/New_York, America/Chicago). Used for scheduling, appointment management, and operational reporting across multiple facilities.
The percentage of the population without health insurance coverage in this region. Used for access-to-care analysis, payer mix forecasting, and community benefit program planning.
High-level classification of the region as urban, suburban, rural, or frontier. Derived from RUCA codes or other urbanization metrics. Used for access-to-care analysis and health equity reporting.
Primary key for npi_registry

business_glossary_term: Practice Location Geographic Region Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to reference.geographic_region. Business justification: NPI registry contains practice location addresses with postal codes that should be normalized to geographic_region for ZIP-based analytics (RUCA codes, HSA/HRR assignments, CMS region mapping). The np
The first name of the authorized official for the organizational provider (Type 2 NPIs only). Used for credentialing verification and organizational accountability.

The last name of the authorized official who is legally responsible for the organizational provider (Type 2 NPIs only). This individual has authority to bind the organization and attest to the accuracy of NPI application information.
The middle name of the authorized official for the organizational provider (Type 2 NPIs only). Optional field for complete identification.
The telephone number of the authorized official for the organizational provider. Used for credentialing verification, attestation confirmation, and regulatory inquiries.

The job title or position of the authorized official within the organization (e.g., CEO, CFO, Administrator, President, Medical Director). Used to verify organizational authority and credentialing compliance.

The date the NPI was deactivated by the provider or CMS. Indicates the provider is no longer actively using this identifier. Used for claims validation, credentialing status checks, and provider directory management.
The IRS Employer Identification Number (EIN) for organizational providers (Type 2 only). Used for tax reporting and organizational identification. Also known as Federal Tax ID.

Indicates whether the NPI is assigned to an individual provider (Type 1) or an organization (Type 2). Type 1 = Individual healthcare provider (physician, nurse, therapist). Type 2 = Healthcare organization (hospital, clinic, group practice, pharmacy).

The date the NPI was originally assigned to the provider by NPPES. Represents the providers initial enrollment in the national provider registry. Critical for credentialing timelines and provider history tracking.

The date the NPI record was last updated in NPPES. Reflects the most recent change to provider demographic information, address, taxonomy, or other registry data. Used to track data freshness and trigger downstream updates.
The city name for the providers mailing address. Used for geographic segmentation and correspondence routing.
The three-letter ISO country code for the providers mailing address (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX). Used for international provider tracking and cross-border claims.
The fax number associated with the providers mailing address. Used for document transmission during credentialing, prior authorization, and claims correspondence.
The first line of the providers mailing address (street address, PO Box, or suite number). Used for official correspondence, credentialing documents, and regulatory communications.
The second line of the providers mailing address (apartment, suite, building, floor). Optional field for additional address detail.
The ZIP code or ZIP+4 code for the providers mailing address. Used for mail delivery, geographic analysis, and service area determination.
The two-letter state or territory code for the providers mailing address (e.g., CA, NY, TX). Used for state-level reporting and regulatory compliance.
The telephone number associated with the providers mailing address. Used for provider contact and verification during credentialing and claims inquiries.

The 10-digit National Provider Identifier assigned by CMS NPPES. Unique identifier for healthcare providers in the United States. This is the authoritative business identifier for provider lookup across claims, credentialing, and directory systems.
The legal business name of the healthcare organization for Type 2 (organizational) NPIs. Examples: hospital name, clinic name, group practice name, pharmacy name.
Alternate name, trade name, or doing-business-as (DBA) name for the healthcare organization. Used when the organization operates under a name different from its legal name.
The three-letter ISO country code for the providers practice location (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX). Used for international provider tracking and cross-border service delivery.

The first line of the providers primary practice location address (street address, suite number). This is the physical location where the provider sees patients or delivers services. Used for provider directories, patient navigation, and service area mapping.
The second line of the providers practice location address (apartment, suite, building, floor). Optional field for additional address detail.
The fax number for the providers practice location. Used for medical records transmission, referral coordination, and prior authorization requests.
The telephone number for the providers practice location. Used for patient appointment scheduling, provider directory listings, and referral coordination.

The primary NUCC Health Care Provider Taxonomy code assigned to this NPI. A 10-digit alphanumeric code that classifies the providers type, classification, and specialization (e.g., 207Q00000X = Family Medicine, 208D00000X = General Practice). This is the providers main specialty for claims submission and network assignment.

Indicates whether the taxonomy code is designated as the providers primary taxonomy. Y = Yes (primary), N = No (secondary). Used to distinguish the main specialty from additional specialties for claims routing and network credentialing.
The professional credential or designation of the individual provider (e.g., MD, DO, RN, DDS, PharmD, PhD, LCSW). Indicates the providers professional qualifications and licensure type.
The legal first name (given name) of the individual healthcare provider for Type 1 NPIs. Used for provider identification, credentialing, and claims submission.
The gender of the individual provider for Type 1 NPIs. M = Male, F = Female. Used for provider demographic reporting and patient preference matching.
The legal last name (family name or surname) of the individual healthcare provider for Type 1 NPIs. Used for provider identification, credentialing, and claims submission.
The middle name of the individual healthcare provider for Type 1 NPIs. Optional field used for complete provider identification.
The name prefix or title for the individual provider (e.g., Dr., Mr., Ms., Rev.). Used for formal provider identification and correspondence.
The name suffix for the individual provider (e.g., Jr., Sr., II, III). Used for complete provider identification and to distinguish between providers with similar names.
An alternate or additional professional credential for the individual provider. Used when a provider holds multiple credentials or has changed credentials.
An alternate or previous first name for the individual provider. Used to track provider name changes and maintain historical continuity.
An alternate or previous last name for the individual provider (e.g., maiden name, former married name). Used to track provider name changes and maintain historical continuity.
An alternate or previous middle name for the individual provider. Used to track provider name changes and maintain historical continuity.
An alternate name prefix for the individual provider. Used to track provider name changes.
An alternate name suffix for the individual provider. Used to track provider name changes.
The date a previously deactivated NPI was reactivated. Indicates the provider has resumed use of this identifier. Used to track provider status changes and maintain accurate active provider lists.

The year-to-date dollar amount or count that has been accumulated toward the benefit threshold. Represents member cost-sharing contributions or service utilization.
Current operational status of the accumulator: active (accumulating), suspended (temporarily paused), closed (benefit period ended), or pending reset (awaiting new benefit year initialization).

The category of benefit accumulation being tracked: individual deductible, family deductible, individual out-of-pocket (OOP) maximum, family OOP maximum, visit limit, or service-specific dollar limit.
Total dollar amount of manual adjustments applied to this accumulator due to claim reversals, appeals, or administrative corrections. May be positive or negative.
The number of adjustment transactions applied to this accumulator. Used for audit trail and data quality monitoring.
The date when the benefit accumulation period ends. Typically December 31 or the plan termination date.
The date when the benefit accumulation period begins. Typically January 1 or the plan effective date for mid-year enrollments.
Calendar year for which the accumulator is tracking benefit utilization. Accumulators typically reset annually on the plan renewal date.
Dollar amount carried over from the previous benefit period, if the plan allows deductible or OOP carryover for services rendered near year-end.
Boolean flag indicating whether this accumulator includes carryover amounts from a prior benefit period. True if carryover_amount is greater than zero.
The tier of coverage for which the accumulator applies: individual, family, employee plus spouse, employee plus children, or full family.
The date and time when this accumulator record was first created in the system. Typically at the start of a new benefit period or upon member enrollment.
Boolean flag indicating whether amounts in this accumulator also count toward other accumulator types. For example, deductible amounts may also count toward OOP max.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this accumulator. Typically USD for US-based healthcare plans.
Boolean flag indicating whether this family-level accumulator uses embedded individual deductibles. True means each family member has an individual deductible within the family deductible.
The date of the most recent adjustment transaction applied to this accumulator. Null if no adjustments have been made.
Service date of the most recent claim that updated this accumulator. Used for recency tracking and accumulator aging analysis.
The date and time when this accumulator record was last modified. Critical for real-time benefit calculation and member portal display.
Indicates whether the accumulator tracks in-network services, out-of-network services, or a combined bucket for both network types.
Free-text field for additional context, special circumstances, or administrative notes related to this accumulator. May include explanations for manual adjustments or unusual accumulation patterns.
Sequential counter indicating which plan year this accumulator represents for the member. Value of 1 for first year, 2 for second year, etc. Used for multi-year trend analysis.
The remaining balance before the threshold is met. Calculated as threshold_amount minus accumulated_amount. Critical for member cost-sharing estimates.
The date when this accumulator was last reset to zero, typically at the start of a new benefit period or upon plan change.
The category of healthcare services to which this accumulator applies: medical, pharmacy, dental, vision, behavioral health, or all services combined.
The plan-defined maximum amount or limit for this accumulator type. Once reached, benefit rules change (e.g., deductible met, OOP max reached).
The date on which the member first met the benefit threshold. Null if threshold has not been met. Used for benefit transition tracking and member communication.
Boolean flag indicating whether the member has met or exceeded the benefit threshold for this accumulator type. True when accumulated_amount >= threshold_amount.
The total number of claim transactions that have contributed to this accumulator balance. Used for utilization pattern analysis.

business_glossary_term: Automatic Coordination of Benefits (COB) Update Enabled
description: Boolean flag indicating whether automatic updates to COB information are enabled through eligibility feeds or third-party vendors. True when automated updates are active.

The type of coordination agreement between payers. Standard COB allows combined benefits up to 100% of charges; non-duplication pays only what primary did not cover; carve-out excludes certain services; maintenance of benefits pays as if primary regardless of other coverage.

The method or rule used to determine the order of benefit responsibility among multiple coverages. Numeric sequence indicating the order of benefit responsibility. 1 = primary, 2 = secondary, 3 = tertiary. Used for claim adjudication sequencing.

The relationship of the member to the subscriber, used in determining COB order under birthday rule or other dependent coverage rules.

business_glossary_term: Affordable Care Act (ACA) Applicable Large Employer (ALE) Indicator
description: Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group meets the ACA definition of an Applicable Large Employer (50 or more full-time equivalent employees). ALEs are subject to the employer shared responsibility mandate and must offer affordable minimum essential coverage or face penalties.
The first line of the employer group's primary business address. Typically includes street number and street name. Used for premium billing, regulatory correspondence, and legal notices.
The second line of the employer group's primary business address. Typically includes suite, floor, or building number. Optional field.
The frequency at which premium invoices are generated and sent to the employer group. Most groups are billed monthly, but some large groups may have quarterly or annual billing cycles.
The city of the employer group's primary business address. Used for geographic rating, network assignment, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.

business_glossary_term: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) Administrator
description: The entity responsible for administering COBRA continuation coverage for terminated employees and qualifying dependents. Payer: health plan administers. Employer: employer self-administers. TPA: third party administrator handles. External vendor: specialized COBRA vendor.
The email address of the primary employer contact for benefits administration. Used for enrollment files, billing statements, and plan communications.
The name of the primary contact person at the employer organization for benefits administration, enrollment, and billing matters. Typically the HR director or benefits manager.
The phone number of the primary employer contact for benefits administration. Used for urgent enrollment issues, billing inquiries, and plan support.
The three-letter ISO country code of the employer group's primary business address. Typically USA for domestic groups. Used for international employer groups and regulatory jurisdiction.
The date and time when this employer group record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
The date on which the employer group's health insurance coverage becomes active and members are eligible for benefits. This is the contract start date.
The number of eligible employees (subscribers) in the employer group, excluding dependents. Used for group size classification, premium calculations, and regulatory reporting.

The percentage of the employee-only premium that the employer pays. The employee pays the remainder. Typical employer contributions range from 50% to 100%. Used for ACA affordability calculations and premium billing.

The federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) assigned by the IRS, also known as the Federal Tax Identification Number. This nine-digit number uniquely identifies the employer for tax reporting and regulatory purposes. Format: XX-XXXXXXX.

business_glossary_term: Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) Plan Indicator
description: Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group's health plan is subject to ERISA federal regulations. True for most private employer plans. False for government and church plans which are ERISA-exempt.

The financial arrangement model for how the employer group funds its health benefits. Fully insured: payer assumes all risk. Self-funded: employer assumes claims risk. Level-funded: hybrid with predictable monthly payments. Minimum premium: employer funds expected claims, payer covers excess. Stop-loss only: employer self-funds with catastrophic reinsurance.

The number of days after the premium due date during which the employer group can make payment without coverage lapsing. Typically 30 days for group coverage. During the grace period, coverage remains active but claims may be pended.
The legal or doing-business-as name of the employer organization that sponsors the health insurance coverage for its employees. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the group.

The externally-known unique business identifier assigned to the employer group by the payer. This is the group number printed on member ID cards and used in all billing and claims transactions. Also known as the policy group number or contract group number.

The total number of enrolled lives (employees and dependents) covered under this employer group. This count determines small group vs. large group classification for regulatory purposes and impacts premium rating methodologies.

The current lifecycle status of the employer group contract. Active: coverage in force. Pending: application submitted, not yet effective. Suspended: temporarily inactive, may be reinstated. Terminated: contract ended by mutual agreement. Cancelled: contract ended by payer. Lapsed: contract ended due to non-payment.

Boolean flag indicating whether this employer group's benefit plan is HSA-qualified (high deductible health plan meeting IRS requirements). If true, employees can contribute pre-tax dollars to a Health Savings Account.

The risk classification based on the employer's industry and occupation mix. Used in underwriting and premium rating. Low: office/professional. Moderate: light manufacturing/retail. High: construction/transportation. Hazardous: mining/heavy industrial.

The minimum percentage of eligible employees that must enroll in the health plan for the group to qualify for coverage. Typically 75% for small groups. Used during initial underwriting and at renewal to prevent adverse selection.

business_glossary_term: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code
description: The six-digit NAICS code that classifies the employer's industry sector. NAICS has largely replaced SIC for statistical and regulatory purposes. Used for industry analysis, risk stratification, and regulatory reporting.
The method by which the employer group remits premium payments to the payer. ACH and wire transfer are most common for large groups. Check and credit card may be used by small groups.

The category of organization that sponsors the health plan. Private employer: for-profit or non-profit business. Union trust: labor union-sponsored plan. Government employer: federal, state, or local government entity. Association: group of small employers. Taft-Hartley: jointly trusteed union-management plan. MEWA: Multiple Employer Welfare Arrangement.
The ZIP code or ZIP+4 code of the employer group's primary business address. Used for geographic rating, network assignment, and premium calculations. Format: XXXXX or XXXXX-XXXX.

The number of months for which the premium rates are guaranteed not to increase. Typically 12 months (annual rate guarantee) for most groups. Some large groups may negotiate multi-year rate guarantees.
The annual date on which the employer group's contract renews. Typically the anniversary of the original effective date. Used for renewal underwriting, rate adjustments, and plan design changes.
The four-digit Standard Industrial Classification code that categorizes the employer's primary line of business or industry. Used for risk assessment, underwriting, and industry benchmarking.

Externally-known patient accounting number assigned to the guarantor account in the EHR revenue cycle or patient accounting system (e.g., Epic Resolute HB guarantor account number). Used by billing staff, financial counselors, and self-pay collection teams to identify and reference the account.

Current lifecycle status of the guarantor account within the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) workflow. Drives billing, collection, and write-off processes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|inactive|collections|bad_debt|deceased|bankruptcy — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
Primary street address line of the guarantor's mailing or billing address. Used for billing statement delivery, collection correspondence, and address verification in RCM workflows.
Secondary address line for the guarantor (apartment, suite, unit, floor, PO Box). Supplements address_line1 for complete mailing address used in billing and collection correspondence.

Self-reported or verified annual gross income of the guarantor in USD. Used for financial assistance (charity care) eligibility screening, sliding-scale fee determination, and payment plan structuring per CMS and ACA financial assistance requirements.

Indicates whether the guarantor account balance has been written off as bad debt in the patient accounting system. Supports financial reporting, bad debt reserve calculations, and RAC audit documentation per GAAP and CMS guidelines.

Indicates whether the guarantor has filed for bankruptcy protection. When True, all collection activities must cease immediately per the automatic stay provisions of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code (11 U.S.C. §362) and the account is flagged for legal review.
City of the guarantor's billing or mailing address. Used in billing statement generation, collection correspondence, and geographic analytics for patient financial services.

Indicates whether the guarantor account has been referred to an external collection agency for bad debt recovery. When True, direct billing and collection activities by the healthcare organization are suspended per FDCPA requirements.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code of the guarantor's billing or mailing address (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX). Supports international patient billing and cross-border financial correspondence.

Timestamp when the guarantor record was first created in the patient accounting system, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format. Supports audit trail requirements, data lineage, and HIPAA compliance documentation.

Date of birth of the guarantor individual in yyyy-MM-dd format. Used for identity verification, eligibility determination for financial assistance programs, and demographic analytics in patient financial services.

Indicates whether the guarantor is deceased. When True, billing and collection workflows are routed to estate billing processes and direct collection outreach is suspended per FDCPA and state probate law requirements.

Indicates whether the guarantor has requested cessation of all billing and collection contact. When True, all outreach activities are suppressed in compliance with FDCPA cease-and-desist provisions and HIPAA patient rights.

Email address of the guarantor used for electronic billing statements (e-statements), payment portal communications, and financial counseling correspondence. Consent for electronic communication must be documented per HIPAA and CAN-SPAM Act.
Name of the guarantor's current employer. Used in financial counseling, self-pay collection assessments, and financial assistance (charity care) eligibility screening to evaluate ability to pay.
Phone number of the guarantor's employer. Used in self-pay collection processes and financial counseling to verify employment status and facilitate payment arrangements.

Current employment status of the guarantor. Used in financial assistance (charity care) eligibility determination, payment plan structuring, and self-pay collection risk stratification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: employed_full_time|employed_part_time|self_employed|unemployed|retired|student|disabled — promote to reference product]

Indicates whether the guarantor has consented to receive electronic billing statements (e-statements) via email or patient portal in lieu of paper statements. Supports paperless billing initiatives and reduces statement delivery costs in RCM.

Calculated Federal Poverty Level (FPL) percentage for the guarantor's household based on annual income and household size. Determines eligibility tier for financial assistance programs, charity care, and sliding-scale discounts per ACA Section 501(r) and CMS guidelines.

Current status of the guarantor's financial assistance (charity care) application. Drives billing hold, discount application, and collection suspension workflows in the RCM system. Supports ACA Section 501(r) compliance reporting.

Type of financial assistance program approved or applied for by the guarantor. Determines the discount percentage, payment schedule, and billing workflow applied to the account. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: charity_care|sliding_scale|payment_plan|hardship|medicaid_pending — promote to reference product]

Legal first (given) name of the guarantor individual. Used in billing correspondence, patient financial counseling communications, and self-pay collection outreach. Protected Health Information (PHI) under HIPAA when linked to patient account data.

Classification of the guarantor indicating whether the responsible party is the patient themselves, a family member, a legal guardian, an estate, or an organization. Determines billing workflow routing and financial counseling approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: self|parent|spouse|legal_guardian|estate|organization — promote to reference product if additional types are required]

Home telephone number of the guarantor. Primary contact channel for billing inquiries, financial counseling outreach, and self-pay collection calls. Stored in compliance with HIPAA and Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) requirements.

Number of individuals in the guarantor's household. Used in conjunction with annual income to determine Federal Poverty Level (FPL) percentage for financial assistance (charity care) eligibility and sliding-scale fee calculations.
Legal last (family) name of the guarantor individual. Used in billing correspondence, collection letters, and identity verification for patient financial services.
Dollar amount of the most recent payment received from the guarantor in USD. Used alongside last_payment_date for payment plan compliance monitoring, collection risk assessment, and RCM reporting.

Date of the most recent payment received from the guarantor toward the outstanding account balance. Used in collection aging analysis, payment plan compliance monitoring, and bad debt risk stratification.

Date on which the most recent billing statement was generated and sent to the guarantor. Used to track billing cycle compliance, manage statement frequency, and support collection escalation timelines in RCM.
Legal middle name or initial of the guarantor individual. Supports identity verification and disambiguation in patient accounting and self-pay collection workflows.

Mobile/cell phone number of the guarantor. Supports SMS billing notifications, payment reminders, and collection outreach. Consent for text messaging must be captured separately per TCPA requirements.

Legal name of the organization acting as guarantor when the responsible party is a business entity, estate, or institution rather than an individual. Populated when guarantor_type is 'organization' or 'estate'.

Agreed monthly payment amount under the guarantor's active payment plan arrangement in USD. Used by RCM billing staff to monitor payment plan compliance and trigger collection escalation if payments are missed.

Indicates whether the guarantor has an active payment plan arrangement for the outstanding account balance. When True, collection activities are suspended and the account follows the payment plan schedule in the RCM system.
ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code of the guarantor's billing or mailing address. Used for billing statement delivery, collection correspondence, and geographic segmentation in patient financial analytics.

Guarantor's preferred method of contact for billing statements, payment reminders, and financial counseling communications. Drives outreach channel selection in RCM workflows and patient financial services.

Describes the guarantor's relationship to the patient as defined in the EHR patient accounting module. Used for financial counseling, billing correspondence, and HIPAA-compliant disclosure of account information. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: self|spouse|parent|child|sibling|grandparent|legal_guardian|other — promote to reference product]

Percentage of the total patient account balance for which this guarantor is financially responsible. Supports scenarios where multiple guarantors share responsibility for a single patient account (e.g., divorced parents of a minor patient). Value range: 0.00 to 100.00.

Date on which the individual or organization was first established as the financial guarantor for the patient account. Marks the effective start of financial responsibility and is used in RCM aging analysis and financial counseling workflows.

Indicates whether the guarantor has provided explicit written consent to receive SMS/text message billing notifications and payment reminders. Required for TCPA compliance before sending automated text messages to the guarantor's mobile phone.

Masked Social Security Number (SSN) of the guarantor, displaying only the last four digits (format: XXX-XX-NNNN). Two-letter US state or territory code of the guarantor's billing or mailing address (e.g., CA, TX, NY). Used for billing correspondence, state-specific financial assistance program eligibility, and regulatory reporting.

Timestamp when the guarantor record was most recently modified in the patient accounting system, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format. Supports change data capture (CDC), audit trail requirements, and Silver layer incremental load processing.
Work telephone number of the guarantor. Used as an alternate contact channel for billing and collection communications when home phone is unavailable. Stored in compliance with HIPAA and TCPA.

Reference to the patient's preferred care facility or clinic location for scheduling outpatient appointments and follow-up care. Used in Epic Cadence and Cerner Millennium to default scheduling to the patient's preferred location.

Reference to the patient's designated Primary Care Physician (PCP). Used for care coordination, referral management, and attribution in value-based care programs such as ACO, HMO, and MIPS. Sourced from Epic EHR registration and Salesforce Health Cloud.
Reference to the patient master record for whom these care and communication preferences are recorded. Links to the patient master identity record.

Reference to the patient's preferred pharmacy for prescription fulfillment. Used by Epic Willow and Cerner PharmNet to route electronic prescriptions (e-prescribing) to the patient's designated pharmacy. Supports medication adherence and care coordination.

Indicates whether the patient has a completed advance directive (e.g., living will, healthcare proxy, POLST) on file with the health system. Triggers clinical alerts in Epic ClinDoc and Cerner PowerChart to ensure care team awareness. Required for CMS Conditions of Participation documentation.

Indicates whether the patient has opted in to receive automated appointment reminders via their preferred communication channel. Drives reminder workflows in Epic Cadence and Cerner Millennium scheduling. Supports no-show reduction and patient access metrics.

Indicates whether the patient has consented to enrollment in care management or disease management programs (e.g., chronic disease management, transitional care, ACO care coordination). Drives population health outreach in Epic Healthy Planet and Salesforce Health Cloud.

Patient's preferred care delivery setting for non-emergency services. Informs care team routing, scheduling, and population health outreach strategies. 'ed' indicates Emergency Department (ED) preference for urgent needs. Supports health equity and SDOH analysis.

Patient's preferred channel for receiving appointment reminders, care instructions, test results, and general health communications. Drives outreach workflows in Epic MyChart, Salesforce Health Cloud, and patient engagement platforms. Supports CAHPS patient experience measurement.

Patient's preferred time of day for receiving outbound communications such as appointment reminders, care management calls, and health coaching outreach. Used by care coordinators and automated outreach systems to optimize contact rates.
Timestamp when the patient preference record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and HIPAA accounting of disclosures. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.

Free-text or coded description of cultural practices, beliefs, or traditions that should be respected during care delivery. Examples include gender-concordant provider preference, traditional healing practices, or specific cultural rituals. Supports culturally competent care and CLAS Standards compliance.

Patient's dietary preferences or restrictions relevant to inpatient meal planning and nutritional care (e.g., vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, gluten-free, diabetic diet). Sourced from EHR registration and nursing assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: vegetarian|vegan|halal|kosher|gluten_free|diabetic|low_sodium|renal — promote to reference product]

Indicates that the patient has requested no outbound contact from the health system for non-clinical communications. When true, suppresses all marketing, outreach, and non-essential communications. Must be honored per HIPAA Right to Restrict and TCPA.

Patient's preferred format for receiving health education materials, discharge instructions, and care plan documents. Drives document generation and delivery in Epic ClinDoc and patient engagement platforms. Supports health literacy and accessibility compliance.

Date from which this set of patient care and communication preferences is considered active and applicable. Enables temporal tracking of preference changes over time and supports preference versioning.

Date on which this set of patient care and communication preferences expires or is superseded. Null indicates the preferences are open-ended and currently active. Supports preference versioning and historical audit.

Indicates whether the patient has expressed a preference to receive care from a provider of the same gender. Used in scheduling and provider assignment workflows to honor patient preferences and support culturally sensitive care delivery.

Assessment of the patient's health literacy level, indicating their ability to understand health information, medication instructions, and care plans. Informs the complexity and format of patient education materials. Supports SDOH analysis and health equity initiatives.

Specific hearing-related accessibility accommodation required by the patient during clinical encounters and communications. Drives accommodation scheduling and facility preparation. Supports ADA compliance and CLAS Standards.

Indicates whether the patient requires professional interpreter services for clinical encounters. When true, triggers interpreter scheduling workflows in Epic Cadence and Cerner Millennium scheduling modules. Supports compliance with Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act.

Specifies the modality of interpreter service preferred or required by the patient. 'sign_language' indicates American Sign Language (ASL) or other signed language interpreter. Informs scheduling and resource allocation in Epic Cadence.
Name or identifier of the staff member, system, or patient who last verified and confirmed the accuracy of the preference record. Supports audit trail and accountability for preference data quality.

Date on which the patient's preferences were last reviewed and confirmed as current by the patient or a designated representative. Supports preference currency tracking and drives re-verification workflows at registration. Aligns with CMS patient engagement requirements.

Indicates whether the patient has opted in to receive health system marketing communications, wellness newsletters, and promotional health content. Distinct from clinical communications. Governed by HIPAA marketing rules and CAN-SPAM Act.

Specific mobility-related accessibility accommodation required by the patient for facility navigation, exam room setup, and transport. Informs facility preparation and scheduling in Epic Cadence. Supports ADA compliance.

Medical Record Number assigned by the facility to uniquely identify the patient within the health system. Used to correlate preferences with clinical and financial records in Epic EHR and Cerner Millennium.

Email address designated by the patient for receiving healthcare notifications, appointment reminders, and portal communications. May differ from the primary contact email on the patient master record. Governed by HIPAA and CAN-SPAM.

Phone number designated by the patient for receiving healthcare notifications, appointment reminders, and care team calls. Expressed in E.164 international format. Governed by TCPA for automated outreach.

Patient's registered organ and tissue donation preference. Sourced from state donor registries and patient registration. Required for CMS Conditions of Participation and UNOS reporting. Informs clinical teams during end-of-life care planning.

Indicates whether the patient is actively enrolled in the patient portal (e.g., Epic MyChart). Portal enrollment enables secure messaging, online scheduling, test result viewing, and medication refill requests. Tracked for CMS Meaningful Use and patient engagement metrics.
Date on which the patient first activated and enrolled in the patient portal. Used to calculate portal engagement duration and for CMS Promoting Interoperability reporting.

Current lifecycle status of the patient preference record. 'active' indicates preferences are current and in use; 'superseded' indicates a newer version exists; 'pending_review' indicates patient-submitted preferences awaiting staff validation.

Full name of the patient's preferred contact person for care coordination communications, appointment reminders, and non-emergency notifications. May be a family member, caregiver, or healthcare proxy. Distinct from the emergency contact on the patient master record.

Relationship of the preferred contact person to the patient. Used to determine appropriate disclosure scope under HIPAA and to contextualize care coordination communications. Required for CLAS Standards compliance and CAHPS survey performance.
Patient preference flag indicating consent to receive PROM surveys via the patient portal or RPM app.

Patient's religious or spiritual affiliation relevant to care delivery, chaplaincy services, dietary restrictions, and end-of-life planning. Informs culturally sensitive care and chaplain referrals. Stored as free text or standardized code per facility policy. Supports CAHPS patient experience and health equity initiatives.

Indicates whether the patient has consented to be contacted for clinical research studies and trials. Drives patient recruitment workflows in research management systems. Supports IRB-compliant research operations and HIPAA Authorization requirements.
